messages:
Incident Bot: [AUTOMATED] Pager fired for tenant=november reserved_pool_id=rp-47 reason=high_tail_latency (p95 > 1.5s)
PagerDuty Bot: Paging oncall: Sam W -> escalation policy: eng-oncall-primary (page id PD-98321)
Sam W: acked PD-98321 :white_check_mark:
Sam W: Looks like reserved pool rp-47 in us-west-2 spiking. Getting a bunch of 5xx + high token-generation latency.
Anya P: grabbing metrics, checking kvcache hit rates + burst queue depth
Leo N: I'm watching the routing dashboard — we got sudden increase in queue length and a drop in available workers for that pool
Rachel G: @Sam any customer-visible errors reported? I see increased 429/503 from the tenant's requests in the logs
Sam W: customer-side 503s yes, rate ~3% of their requests in the last 2m. SLA at risk if sustained.
Anya P: kvcache hit rate for rp-47 down from 78% -> 32% over last 10m; eviction storm maybe after a large model update?
Leo N: worker pods showing memory pressure and OOM-killing some grpc workers in that pool. node metrics attached: cpu 60%, mem 92% on 3 nodes
Sam W: running a quick query: `kubectl describe pod rp-47-worker-3` shows repeated eviction: "oomkilled: memory" and restart count 4
oncall-bot: Automatic mitigation suggestion: enable burst-balance for rp-47 (add +2 burst nodes) OR route low-priority traffic to fallback pool rp-shared-lowprio
Sam W: I'm going to enable burst nodes and route low-priority class to fallback. Doing it now.
Sam W: `infractl reserved add-burst --pool rp-47 --count 2`
PagerDuty Bot: PD-98321 note: Sam W requested adding burst capacity
Leo N: routing change in place: low-priority route -> rp-shared-lowprio ; generating config diff: `route_priority: low -> rp-shared-lowprio`
Anya P: deploying kv cache warmup for rp-47; sending warm prefixes to bring hit rate up
Rachel G: monitoring customer errors as we do this — spike should drop within minutes if kvcache warms and burst nodes come up
Sam W: burst nodes provisioned, but one failed to join due to docker image pull error (timeout). Restarting provisioner.
Kai M: I can help with image pull — repo had a transient registry throttling. Retrying with alternate mirror.
Sam W: mirror worked, second node joined. Current pool nodes: 5 -> 7
Anya P: kvcache hit rate creeping back: 32% -> 54% in last 90s
Leo N: queue depth dropping from 420 -> 110, p95 latency trending down from 2.1s -> 1.1s
Sam W: customer 503 rate down to 0.8% — still above baseline but improving.
PagerDuty Bot: PD-98321 update: incident state: acknowledged by Sam W; escalation paused
Rachel G: recommend we keep low-priority routing for another 15m and keep burst nodes until pool stabilizes. Also want to create a post-incident ticket to investigate kvcache eviction root cause and registry throttling during burst provisioning
Sam W: Agreed. Creating incident bridged note and tagging SRE: `INC-2026-119-november-rp47`
Sam W: handoff in 20m to @Kai M for steady-state monitoring — I'll stay on for 10 more to confirm stability
Kai M: ack — will take over at +20m. If p95 > 1.2s or 5xx > 1% escalate to infra-oncall
Anya P: capturing commands run and logs: `kubectl logs rp-47-provisioner` , `infractl reserved list --pool rp-47` , snapshotting prom graphs to the incident ticket
Sam W: quick note for the ticket: customer impacted = tenant 'november' ; initial impact window 2623456789 -> ongoing; mitigations = +2 burst nodes, low-priority routing, kv cache warmup; next steps = postmortem, improve registry mirror fallback during autoscale, analyze cache churn after model updates
PagerDuty Bot: PD-98321 closed (manual) by Sam W :white_check_mark:
Sam W: closing thread here, transferring notes into INC-2026-119-november-rp47 and tagging product/support for customer comms
Kai M: I'll monitor for 1 hour then close incident ticket if steady.
Rachel G: thanks team — nice fast mitigation. :thumbsup:
Kai M: joining incident bridge now for handoff
Sam W: handing over.
